svg.title: TreeLab: the linear control still wins
svg.desc: Full real-data pruning path, held-out metrics, and one complete selected-tree prediction route. One fixed split, not a deployment claim.

g.text: TreeLab / pruning reduces complexity, not every error
From-scratch CART on UCI white wine. Same-fit least squares remains the stronger held-out control.
1. Group-disjoint source split, selected without held-out targets
4,898 rows / 3,961 exact feature groups. Fit 2921; validation 1008; test 969.
Exact copies stay together. Near copies, batch overlap and future-distribution shift are not ruled out.
2. Every weakest-link state is retained; validation chooses 19 leaves
290 states: normalized fitting SSE + alpha x leaf count. No test curve is used for selection.
3. One complete route, not feature causality
First test row 1: leaf 332, 475 fitting rows, prediction 5.31579; recorded score 6.
One target-blind hash-group split. Ordinal scores treated as numeric. No confidence, safety or SOTA claim.
Data: Cortez et al. (2009), UCI DOI 10.24432/C56S3T, CC BY 4.0. Derived metrics and chart; not endorsed.
Established CART / weakest-link pruning. Binary64 arithmetic and finite oracles, not exact all-input proofs.
